learningObjectives: Explain the physiological or methodological basis of EEG Source Localisation.
Apply EEG Source Localisation to technically valid clinical interpretation.
Identify artifacts, confounds and limits that could alter conclusions.
Communicate findings without exceeding the evidence or professional scope.

mechanismMap.label: Core concept
mechanismMap.detail: Inverse methods estimate source distributions that could produce observed scalp fields.

mechanismMap.label: Mechanism
mechanismMap.detail: The inverse problem has no unique solution without constraints. Head models, electrode positions, regularisation and source space strongly shape results.

mechanismMap.label: Clinical integration
mechanismMap.detail: Can complement expert EEG interpretation and research when uncertainty is explicit.

mechanismMap.label: Boundary condition
mechanismMap.detail: Displaying a 3D source image can create unjustified anatomical confidence.

quizBank.question: Which statement best captures EEG Source Localisation?
options: Inverse methods estimate source distributions that could produce observed scalp fields.
It provides a stand-alone psychiatric diagnosis
It is unaffected by state and artifact
Its interpretation requires no clinical context
quizBank.explanation: Inverse methods estimate source distributions that could produce observed scalp fields.

quizBank.question: What is the safest clinical principle for EEG Source Localisation?
options: Integrate raw signal quality, state, method and clinical context
Assume a coloured map shows exact anatomy
Treat statistical rarity as proof of disorder
quizBank.explanation: EEG and QEEG interpretation requires converging evidence, technical validity and clinical context.

quizBank.question: Which error is most important to avoid in EEG Source Localisation?
options: Displaying a 3D source image can create unjustified anatomical confidence.
quizBank.explanation: Displaying a 3D source image can create unjustified anatomical confidence.

reviewPrompts.answer: The inverse problem has no unique solution without constraints. Head models, electrode positions, regularisation and source space strongly shape results.
Can complement expert EEG interpretation and research when uncertainty is explicit.
Displaying a 3D source image can create unjustified anatomical confidence.
Source localisation is model-based inference, not direct imaging.
